text:
anya: heads up — after the routing change last night i'm seeing a consistent hit-rate delta between regions (eu ~62% vs us ~88%) for our seeded prompt set.

matt: ouch. is that for the whole model fleet or just the small-llama family?

anya: small-llama family specifically, but the pattern shows up on a few quantized variants too. p50 latencies are fine, p95 on eu spikes when misses cascade into cold kv fetches.

sanjay: can you paste the perf snippet?

anya: paste below — this is from perf-agent at 02:12 UTC (shortened):
```
model: small-llama-q4
region: eu-west
routing: region-prefer -> fallback-any
kv_fetch_miss_cost_ms: 12.3
p50: 12.1ms
p95: 189.7ms  # baseline was ~95ms yesterday
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
```

leah: looks like misses are hitting the cold-replica path, which does a sync read before serving. did we change replication policy?

matt: yes — we flipped the geo-sync window to async for background replication to reduce write latency (commit v2.14.0). that might delay hot-key propagation.

anya: exactly. i traced a request where route affinity sent to eu-edge but the hot key lived on us-primary and replication lag was 7s. fallback routed to on-demand fetch and kernel path took small-batch fallback.

infra-bot: deploy v2.14.0 rolled to eu cluster @ 2026-02-14T01:03Z (canary->prod).

sanjay: i suspect two contributors: 1) replication async window >> routing TTL so hot keys not available locally and 2) small-batch kernel fallback increases p95 when kv fetch extra hop.

leah: proposal: make routing fall back to regional read-replica first (stale-while-revalidate) for up to 1s, and for hot prefix keys mark them "geo-pinned" so replication is prioritized. also reduce small-batch fallback threshold for eu for a short canary.

matt: +1. Also we should instrument kernel-selection traces in the hot path so we can see when we pick the small-batch kernel vs packed-kernel. add a tag `kernel_choice` to trace spans.

anya: i ran an A/B with geo-pinned for top-1k prefixes and saw eu hit-rate jump to 85% with p95 back to ~100ms. short test only 30m.

ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-212: "eu kv replication lag impacting seeded prompt hit-rate" — assigned to eng-runtime.

matt: next actions: 1) revert async replication window to previous value for canary regions, 2) enable kernel_choice tracing, 3) experiment with route affinity TTLs and stale-while-revalidate = 1s, 4) run a 6hr geo-pinning trial on top-2k prefixes.

leah: i'll own 1 & 3; sanjay will own 2 & 4. can we also dump a compact heatmap of prefix entropy per region to decide which prefixes to pin?

anya: yes — i already have a script that produces a csv. sample header: `prefix,eu_hits,us_hits,entropy,avg_len`. dropping it in #eng-runtime-analysis after this thread.

sanjay: for the trace schema: use `kernel_choice` = ["packed","small_batch","fallback_kv"], `kv_path` = ["local","replica","on_demand"], and include `replication_lag_ms` for events where kv_path != local.

matt: good. timeline — can we get the first canary with reverted window and traces in 2 hours?

leah: yes, i'll schedule the rollback to eu-canary at 04:30Z and enable trace flags. will post results.

anya: thanks. starting heatmap export now. will report back with csv and the 30m A/B results. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: rollback scheduled: v2.14.0 -> v2.13.8 on eu-canary @ 04:30Z.

matt: great. after that if the hit-rate gap closes we can fast-follow for other regions but with a more principled geo-pinning policy.

leah: one more note — if we geo-pin too aggressively we risk stranding cold keys on fewer nodes; we'll set an eviction TTL for geo-pinned keys to 12h and reevaluate.

anya: agreed. short-term mitigation + observability first, policy tuning next.

sanjay: i'll add dashboards: kernel_choice breakdown, kv_path breakdown, replication_lag histogram, and a per-prefix heatmap.

anya: okay closing thread for now, will update when logs/csv are uploaded.
